messages:
Jordan (customer): Hey team — after we flipped traffic to the on-prem proxy + interface endpoint, our app started getting intermittent 502/504s to Redwood API and a big spike in billable requests (x8). Can we triage?

lee_support: sorry you're hitting this — can you share a quick repro and whether Private DNS was enabled on your VPC endpoint?

Jordan (customer): Repro is simple: curl to our app which calls Redwood via interface endpoint. Happens under load. Private DNS ON. curl -vv shows TLS handshake sometimes failing then client retries.

priya_eng: thanks. two quick hypotheses: 1) TLS SNI/host mismatch when proxy rewrites Host header, 2) egress allowlist or STS metadata blocked causing token refresh retries.

sam_infra: also check SNAT behavior — on-prem proxy + NAT can change source IPs, breaking endpoint routing or health checks and causing backend 502s.

lee_support: can you paste a minimal curl -vv from a failing request (redact keys)? Also tcpdump/traceroute from the proxy if possible.

Jordan (customer): here's a redacted curl output: 

-----
* Connected to vpce-abc123.execute-api.internal (10.0.2.15) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS 1.2 connection using ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
* Fatal TLS error: handshake failure
* Closing connection 0
-----

lee_support: that handshake failure looks intermittent — can you run openssl s_client to check SNI?

Jordan (customer): ran: openssl s_client -connect vpce-abc123.execute-api.internal:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com
Server certificate:
    subject: CN=api.redwood.example.com
    subjectAltName: DNS:api.redwood.example.com

lee_support: OK cert looks fine when SNI matches. If proxy or ALB strips or rewrites SNI/Host then the backend might return a cert that doesn't match and clients retry.

priya_eng: another angle — are you terminating TLS at the proxy or passing through? If terminating, ensure proxy presents the correct Host header when connecting to the interface endpoint backend. If passing through, check that ALPN and SNI are preserved.

sam_infra: share route table and security group attached to the interface endpoint subnets. Also confirm no SNAT on the path back to our endpoint — if replies go via NAT with different source, our endpoint health checks/ACLs could reject and you see 502s.

Jordan (customer): route table has 0.0.0.0 -> onprem-nat (tgw) for egress, SG allows outbound 443 to vpce. NACL is open. Proxy terminates TLS and re-opens to vpce.

lee_support: proxy terminating TLS + re-issuing to vpce is a common source of host/SNI mismatch. Two quick tests: 1) bypass proxy for one client and see if errors stop, 2) from proxy, curl to VPC endpoint with Host header set to api.redwood.example.com:

curl -v -H 'Host: api.redwood.example.com' https://vpce-abc123.execute-api.internal/endpoint

priya_eng: also check your proxy TLS profile. Some proxies negotiate older ciphers leading to handshake failures under load. Grab `ssltap` or `openssl s_client -connect` during a failure window.

Jordan (customer): ran the Host header curl — request succeeds every time when Host header is set. When proxy uses backend hostname it fails ~20% under load.

sam_infra: that confirms host header rewrite problem. Proxy must pass the original Host (or SNI) when connecting to vpce. If it rewrites to vpce internal name, backend cert mismatch -> client retries -> billing spike.

lee_support: for immediate mitigation: set proxy upstream to use SNI and Host = api.redwood.example.com, or configure a TCP passthrough for that path. We'll also whitelist your proxy IPs on our side to reduce rate-limiting churn while you fix.

Jordan (customer): thanks — can you whitelist? Our ephemeral source IPs are NATed via tgw; I'll send the public egress CIDR.

oncall-bot: Note: incident created #INC-20230624-47 — support assigned lee_support, priya_eng.

priya_eng: follow-up: please confirm whether your proxy is rewriting Host header for path-based routing. If you need a config sample for nginx upstream: 

-----
upstream redwood_api {
    server vpce-abc123.execute-api.internal:443;
}
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    proxy_pass https://redwood_api;
    proxy_set_header Host api.redwood.example.com;
    proxy_ssl_server_name on; 
    proxy_ssl_name api.redwood.example.com;
}
-----

sam_infra: also double-check that your healthchecks to the proxy/backend aren't causing retries — aggressive healthcheck timeouts can trigger traffic reshuffle that increases transient 502s.

Jordan (customer): implementing Host passthrough now. Will report back in 30m. Appreciate the quick triage.

lee_support: sounds good. post the egress CIDR for temporary whitelist and we can monitor for cost anomalies. Recommend also enabling Private DNS fallback to ensure internal host resolves consistently. :thumbsup:
